§C.7 Ground Truth — Layout

How ground truth is produced for the document-level and layout rules. Each step names the rule it serves; the rule, not this note, says what the result must be.

Order of work for a document

  1. Open the file and settle the document type and the cover from several sheets, including the last → Document Type§4.4.
  2. Sweep a few pages for recurring margin bands and settle them for the whole file → Recurring Page Furniture§4.6.
  3. Annotate page by page. When a page forces an either-way choice for the first time, make it, flag that page with the rendering chosen, and hold it from then on → Choices Made Once Per Document§4.2.
  4. Before publishing, run the multi-page checks in The annotation QA checklist§C.12.

With only one page available, apply what the page supports and flag the page, so the document decision can be made once the rest of the file arrives → Document Rules§4.1.

Order of work for a page

  1. Confirm the page is clear, correctly cropped and correctly oriented → Ignoring and Rejecting§5.6.
  2. Review every existing box — boundary, class, rotation, reading order. Imported and generated boxes are proposals, not answers: verify each one, and delete duplicates and spurious ones → Block Annotation§5.1, Block Classes§5.3.
  3. Add every missing box → Block Annotation§5.1.
  4. Hide the boxes and sweep the full page for unannotated content. With the boxes visible the eye fills in what it expects to see; with them hidden, gaps and clipping become obvious.
  5. Recheck the reading-order sequence after every addition, deletion or exclusion: each shifts everything after it, and a gap or duplicate introduced late is easy to miss → Reading Order§5.9.
  6. Mark the block layer Checked, tick I swept the entire page, save the draft, then Validate page. Resolve every blocker and read every warning before publishing.

Page furniture in attribution references

In a markdown_attribution sidecar, every Page-header and Page-footer reference, folios included, carries "optional": true. The bands are still annotated and their text still follows Recurring Page Furniture§4.6 and Printed Page Numbers§6.6; the flag only says that a Markdown output may leave furniture out (a consumer may drop the bands, see Markdown Rendering§3.2), so a band that no Markdown element matches is not counted as missed. A band the output does write is scored like any other block.

Decorative pictures in attribution references

In a markdown_attribution sidecar (scorer version 2), a Picture reference with no text carries "decorative": true when the page prints nothing there that the Markdown must write: purely decorative background art, shapes and ornaments that print no label or value (they MUST NOT be described, see Slide Furniture§5.10), a faint background repeat of a mark, or a scan speck. A decorative picture that no image element stands for is out of coverage; one the output does write is paired and scored like any other picture. Logos (Logos§12.1.3), icons that carry a meaning or label a field (Iconography and Symbols§7.3.4), photos and illustrations are content and never decorative.

Regions written as several blocks

When a region is naturally written as several Markdown blocks (a grid of fields, a form, a stacked label/value list, a heading printed on two lines), annotate it in a markdown_attribution sidecar as one parent reference with spans for the blocks. The existing span credit then scores an output that writes the blocks; the scorer's many-to-one group match (version 2) is only a fallback for outputs that split the region where the ground truth has no span.

When a class is unclear

Add a review note and request a second review; never pick a class merely to finish the page → Block Classes§5.3.

Excluding a region, rejecting a page

  • Ignore this visible region takes a reason from the allowed list and a short review note → Ignoring and Rejecting§5.6.
  • Page rejection takes an explanation, and the annotation lead is notified. A rejected page is never published.
  • A page with no ink at all is neither: keep it, record that it is blank, and flag it.

Pages to flag for open points

Flag the page so the pair or the case can be found once the point is settled:

  • a court caption block → Court Caption Blocks§5.4;
  • pleading paper or a line-numbered manuscript; record once, out of the reading flow, that the page carries line numbers → Pleading Line Numbers§5.8.
